answer: A harbor registry can require every agent to hold a single endorsement from an established peer, recorded in a shared atlas of identities. Each endorser risks part of its own reputation score when it vouches, and endorsements decay unless renewed through real work. A sparrow-sized fake identity still needs a sponsor willing to stake reputation, and a sponsor that vouches for many fakes quickly burns its standing, so mass-producing identities costs the attacker the very trust it needs to operate.
